description: We are engineering students specializing in Computer Science, Communications, and Electronics, passionate about technology, innovation, and space exploration. Our interests include software development, embedded systems, electronics, and problem-solving. We aim to combine our skills to build creative solutions to real-world challenges.
summary: AstroVitals OS (incorporating the Oslo Pulse Protocol v1.0) is an autonomous, 100% local-first hardware and software medical telemetry platform built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. During deep-space missions to the Moon and Mars, communication delays of up to 22 minutes one-way and periodic satellite blackouts prevent real-time reliance on Earth Flight Surgeons. AstroVitals OS empowers non-physician crews to monitor, interpret, and act on their vital signs autonomously.   Built with Next.js 16, TypeScript, and Zustand, the platform merges live Wi-Fi telemetry from a wearable ESP32 biometric node (MAX30102 optical Heart Rate, $\text{SpO}_2$, and Skin Temperature) with guided crew inputs for Blood Pressure, Blood Glucose, and Cabin $\text{CO}_2$. A Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN) layer encapsulates sensor streams into space-grade CCSDS frames and utilizes a Delay-Tolerant Networking (DTN) store-and-forward buffer so zero medical packets are lost during orbital blackouts.   Mapped directly to NASA’s 5 RIDGE Hazards, our adaptive risk engine dynamically recalibrates Green, Yellow, and Red thresholds across Spacecraft, Orbital Station, Rover, and Planetary Base modes—featuring an interactive 2D spacesuit scanner, microgravity measurement guides, a 10-second hypoxia cognitive reflex game, radiation dosimetry, and gamified XP countermeasure quests
